source.author: cic
source.text: at hoc in eo M. Crasso, quem semel ait in vita risisse Lucilius, non contigit, ut ea re minus , ut ait idem, vocaretur.
source.text_original: at hoc in eo M. Crasso, quem semel ait in vita risisse Lucilius, non contigit, ut ea re minus ἀγέλαστος, ut ait idem, vocaretur.
source.text_english: But this did not happen in the case of M. Crassus, whom Lucilius says laughed only once in his life, so that on that account he was not for that reason, as the same writer says, called any the less.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Catonem quoque illum dico censorium et uestrae quondam urbis principem , qui in extrema aetate Graecas litteras non erubuit censor nec desperauit senex discere et M. Crassum semel in uita scribit risisse Lucilius.
reuse.text_original: Catonem quoque — illum dico censorium et uestrae quondam urbis principem —, qui in extrema aetate Graecas litteras non erubuit censor nec desperauit senex discere **************** et M. Crassum semel in uita scribit risisse Lucilius.
reuse.text_english: I mean that same Cato, the censor and once the leading man of your city, who in his extreme old age did not blush, as censor, at Greek letters and did not despair of learning as an old man; and Lucilius writes that M. Crassus laughed only once in his life.
